params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.text:
ROADCLOSE PASS. TOKEN RELEASED. Backup before the first write: world_backups/world-Ulfsland-backup-2026-09-16_13-28-04.tgz. Saved at seq 1678 with a verified postcondition (4 zone centres, 1 _TerrainCompiler each).
T1-portalhub-temple: clearing COMPLETED -- 17 further cylinders emitted (seq 1644-1655, 1657-1661), 199 more objects removed; 46 of 47 cylinders now recorded, 470 of 3,888 censused objects matched as verified-deleted, 18 clearable objects still standing inside the derived clear width (all in the six cylinders the POI/blocker gate shrank or skipped, and the batter clipped around them: 43 samples clipped beside a live placed object). Battered as a repair of seq 413 -> terrain_write seq 1666. Transverse before -> after: carriageway 1 m p50 0.320 -> 0.158, max 4.150 -> 1.485; own earthwork p95 1.419 -> 0.781, max 5.548 -> 3.626; over-grade fraction 0.1004 -> 0.0367 against 0.8613 (0.7813 batter grade + 0.08 diagonal); legacy band p50 1.365 -> 0.781, which is the design grade exactly. Longitudinal 8 m gradient 0.2407 (limit 0.781, the 38 deg slide angle); the 1 m figure beside it, a different quantity, is 1.4112. zone_ctrl 1 of 1 in all nine zones, 0 past the +/-8 m clamp, 0 below water 30.0. 37 over-grade pairs of 6,316 unexplained by a recorded clip, 10 stations, largest adjacent run 7 -- the same family as the accepted T4 (32/10/4) and T9 (14/9/4). 21 interstice rays at the T13 junction left ungraded and RECORDED (profile difference 3.15-4.53 m against 0.01-0.61 m the grade can absorb across the gap): never grade two roads into each other.
S1-portalhub-brgs2: censused 2,351 objects over 7 cells, 1 cylinder cleared, 0 clearable left inside the clear width. Battered as a repair of seq 417 -> terrain_write seq 1675: 91 paved + 65 shoulder + 26 batter samples over 2 zones, cut -1.441 fill 1.076. Carriageway 1 m p50 0.305 -> 0.134, max 1.025; own earthwork p50 0.249 p95 0.630 max 0.698 over 39 pairs, over-grade fraction 0.0 -- VERDICT pass. Walls left worst 0.760 -> 0.478 m. Longitudinal 8 m 0.4374 (limit 0.781), 1 m figure 1.75. zone_ctrl 1 of 1 in both zones, 0 past the clamp, 0 below water. THE JUNCTION CREST IS UNTOUCHED AS RECORDED: 22 samples refused beside a protected piece and a 1.5 m gap at (-315.3, 229.3) with fill -1.067 at its edge -- bridge-s2-portalhall-strait's 156 protected pieces measure worst applied delta 0.000 m in this write's own location_check, so the bridge is provably unmoved and the 0.37-0.44 m crest is left exactly as ruled.
THE WRITE-TIME PAD-FOOTPRINT GUARD IS LANDED in ledger/writer.py::Ledger._pad_footprint_check, wired into _cross_record_checks beside the zone-clobber and flatten-FORBIDDEN invariants, so it fires for every appender and not only for ribbon.py. A pad is recognised by SHAPE (pad_w/pad_d + target_y, the schema's own target_y-XOR-profile distinction) not by a role list; its footprint is pos + pad_w/2+apron x pad_d/2+apron, with the position resolved from the site's sibling records because a pad's terrain_write carries no pos at all (all 50 resolve, 0 do not); AND the ground the pad itself levelled, because stenvik-stonehouse-1 seq 272 authored 165 samples of which only 60 are inside its 11.0 x 15.0 m rectangle. PROVEN BOTH WAYS OFFLINE BEFORE ANY WRITE, on a sandbox copy of the chain: it FIRES on the no-rewind T8 re-repair fixture built from the ledger's own blobs (316 samples across 4 pads -- stenvik-beehive-1 166, stenvik-house-3 91, stenvik-stonehouse-1 39, wt-town 20 -- naming the count, the rectangle and the claim that holds each sample), and it PASSES T1's and S1's new writes at the portal hall pad, which is where the road legitimately terminates. It also PASSES 11 of the 15 landed road claims and reports 91 genuinely contested samples on the other four (T8 58, T9 17, W5 16) as pre-existing state, not as anything this pass did.
RULE 1 IS NOW AUTHORSHIP, NOT A NAME FILTER, and the name filter was wrong in the direction nobody had measured. Dropping a segment's own zone entries cures T8 and CAUSES the mirror defect: the portal hall's pad seq 801 unioned S1's carriageway forward bit-identically (sample (-300, 214) is -1.694 in both blobs), so with S1's own records dropped the hall became the first claim to hold those samples and read as their author. foreign_at then answered portal-hall#801 over the whole 30.6 m ramp, the rasteriser refused all 215 carriageway samples and stamped ZERO: the first surface a player walks off a portal was unrepairable, and no name filter can fix it because the laundered copy is under the HALL's name. applied.py::Applied.zone now composes an AUTHOR per sample -- the last claim whose value DIFFERED from what the claims before it had composed -- beside the holder, holders()/owners_at()/foreign_at()/sample() all answer by author, and nothing is dropped from the composition, so a carried copy can never become a first write. Both directions fall out of one measurement. ribbon.py's rule-2 guard and the new ledger guard were both rewritten onto it; before that, ribbon's guard refused 156 of S1's own samples to the hall at positions like (-302, 212) that are outside the hall's rectangle entirely.
T4's CLIFF, DIAGNOSED AND NOT YET REPAIRED, and the cause is one constant. APPROACH_MAX_M was 11.5 m on the stated reasoning that 'the apply clamp is +/-8 m, so the largest step the road can possibly owe a pad is 8 m, and 8/0.781 = 10.24 m of run removes it at grade'. THE PREMISE IS FALSE: the clamp bounds one terrain_write against the GENERATED height and does not bound the step between a road's profile and a pad's levelled datum, because the pad spends a clamp budget of its own in the other direction -- T4's measured residual at stenvik is -10.414 m, 2.4 m larger than the largest step the constant assumes can exist. With the run capped at 11.5 m the ramp grade saturates at BATTER_GRADE, which IS the slide limit, so the last stretch is unwalkable by construction and T4's 8 m gradient measured 0.8849. Landed: APPROACH_MIN_M 11.5 as a FLOOR, APPROACH_RUN_CAP_M 240.0 as the ceiling the function's own docstring already claimed, and ribbon.approach_reach_m deriving the run as step/design bounded by the segment's own length -- so the grade lands ON the design 8 % whenever the run is there. MEASURED offline after the change: T12 2.991 -> 0.032 m over 23 nodes (was 0.070 over 11) and T4 2.824 -> 0.656 m over 114 nodes. The T12 regression this constant was shrunk to avoid cannot recur because a claim now REQUIRES a non-zero live delta -- somebody's earthwork, not somebody's intention.
AND THE REAL T4 CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN THE RAMP, MEASURED, NOT FIXED: stenvik's keep-out in settlements/sites.yaml is pad_radius_m 100.0, a DISTRICT radius, and the rasteriser treats it as a pad. T4 therefore writes NOTHING for 293.9 m of centreline at (544.8, 809.2) and the step across that gap is -8.491 m. The foundations that must not move are the per-building site_pads (26.1, 20.3, 16.0, 11.0 m), and stenvik-house-3 at (606.5, 938.8) is 113 m from the town centre -- OUTSIDE the 100 m disc -- so roads already write inside the district and the guard that now protects the real footprints is exactly what makes doing so safe. Re-solving T4's profile alone cannot close a 294 m unwritten gap; the road has to be RASTERISED through the district, skipping only the building rectangles. That is the repair, it is one change to what pad_keepouts means, and it was not attempted tonight rather than attempted half-way.
NETWORK-WIDE, the two closing numbers, read off the ledger and applied.py rather than off any one report. TREES STILL STANDING INSIDE THE DERIVED CLEARING WIDTH: 278 per-segment records over the 13 segments whose pre-clearing censuses survive, 268 distinct ZDO ids once corridors that overlap are deduplicated -- T4 85, T5 75, S8 33, T1 18, S7 15, T13 13, T10 12, W5 11, T8 9, W10 4, T9 3, S12 0, S1 0. Every one of them is inside a cylinder the POI/blocker gate shrank or skipped, is recorded in that cylinder's skip reason, and had the batter clipped around it rather than under it. T12-wtspawn-temple and T3-temple-meadhall were cleared (26 and 28 cylinders in the chain) in a session whose census files no longer exist, so 268 is a LOWER BOUND over 13 of 15 segments and that is stated rather than rounded up. WORST TRANSVERSE 1 m STEP ANYWHERE ON THE NETWORK: 7.749 m on S7-stathub-wtnorth, unchanged by its repair; then T4 6.774, T9 6.752, T5 and T13 5.817. The worst on a CARRIAGEWAY is T4's 6.556 m, also unchanged, and correctly so -- those samples are stenvik's pad and the pad wins inside its footprint.

approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.note: persist the T4-meadhall-stathub repair of seq 1158: WALKABLE, 8 m gradient 0.8849 -> 0.4717, 2456 -> 2938 of 3109 centreline stations on written road, 0 samples past the +/-8 m clamp. Landed after fixing writer._pad_footprint_check to resolve pad authorship to the EFFECTIVE (latest) author per Main's ruling.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

unexplained_over_grade.adjacency_method: MEASURED on the STEP POSITION (`step_xz`, the midpoint between the two censused samples) at a matched lateral, over the subset this write actually made -- a step the GENERATED surface already has at the same two points is the hillside. Clustering on the station centre instead reads a bend cross section as a cliff, and counting natural steps reads a hillside as one.

repair_before.when: off the LIVE blobs, RoadWalkable pass

approach_reach_solve.why: no claim on this segment, so there is no approach to solve

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED on T12-wtspawn-temple and T3-temple-meadhall. clear.py::plan_removals pulled a removal disc in to min(nearest_blocker) - TERRAIN_SPREAD_M, which is the right RULE with the wrong GEOMETRY: a blocker near the centre erases the disc. T12's derived disc at (77.43,-67.43) r 12.57 m met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, so the disc that was sent (seq 937 and 952) had radius 3.84 m, removed 4 objects and left 14 standing inside the derived clearing width -- 13 of which this segment's own terrain write then BURIED, worst 3.818 m. Coverage on T12 went 5 of 22 targeted to 16 of 22; T3 went to 15 of 15.

params.method: MEASURED with ribbon.stamp's new per-ray `ray_end_at` record -- station arc, side, termination lateral and cause for every ray, which is the unit that terminates. Main's test, run on the termination lateral against station: T12 adjacent-station jump p50 0.71 m p95 2.12 m over 277 pairs, 2 sign reversals over 1 m; T3 p50 0.64 m p95 1.41 m over 825 pairs, 10 reversals. EVERY reversal on both segments is one ray clipped `steeper_than_batter` -- a RECORDED cause the transverse census already consults -- flanked by rays that met natural ground, and ZERO reversals have no recorded clip at the dip. So the locus varies continuously and the adjacent clips are adjacent because the hillside is. A first attempt that bucketed WRITTEN SAMPLES into 1 m station bins instead reported a 5.611 m sawtooth on T12 at station 268: that measures lattice aliasing on a diagonal centreline, not ray termination, and its verdict is withdrawn.

params.method: MEASURED, not inherited: a fresh live per-cell census of all 15 built segments (clear.census_zoned, 1,216 cells, unscoped findObjects at five y levels), filtered to clearable prefabs inside each station's own derived clear width, with buried/floating/flush taken off applied.py's live union. The previous figure was 305 with 37 on T12 and T3. THE SKIP-REASON CLAIM IS FALSE FOR 262 OF 268 AND IS CORRECTED HERE: zero of 1,731 ledger records carry per-cylinder skip detail. `plan_removals` builds `skipped_detail` (blocker, allowed radius, object count) and `emit` builds `cylinders_skipped_at_emit`, and NEITHER IS APPENDED -- the only skip information in the chain is a COUNT inside each segment's `road_surface_clearing_plan` observe. params.method: MEASURED with ribbon.stamp's `ray_end_at` (station arc, side, termination lateral, cause -- per RAY, the unit that terminates). A reversal counts only above the COMPILER LATTICE DIAGONAL, sqrt(2) x 1 m SCALE + 1 cm: a diagonal ray that ends one member short of its neighbour differs by exactly 1.4142 m for sampling reasons alone, and a 1.0 m threshold read T5 and T13 as defects on amplitudes of 1.414, 1.414 and 1.682 m -- my own false alarm, from a threshold picked rather than derived. A reversal is a DEFECT candidate only when the dipping ray's cause is `lattice_end`, the one exit of the five that neither files a `_clip` nor reaches natural ground; enumerating the accounted causes by hand instead gave a second false alarm by omitting `water_edge`, the clip class that must never be graded.

The locus varies continuously: the adjacent clips are adjacent because the hillside is. Main's question is answered and closed; the transverse census's ADJACENT flag is a screening signal, not a verdict.
value.still_open: THREE segments have a genuine jagged termination: T8-stenvik-wttown 4 of 9 reversals unaccounted, worst 9.192 m at station 223 side +1 (laterals 4.24, 13.44, 4.24); T13-temple-harboursouth 1 of 1, 1.682 m at station 199 side +1; W5-brgs1-wsouth 1 of 8. params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T4_meadhall_stathub

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

params.method: MEASURED -- the per-cylinder disposition of THIS clearing pass, appended at the end of the same session that sent the removals: the plan's blocked-tile skips, the location gate's per-cylinder skips, the skips this call's own immediately-prior live census forced, the blocker-clear sub-discs actually sent with the derived parent disc each one is a subset of, and every object left inside the derived clearing width named by prefab + world position with the blocker that binds it.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

This cylinder's parent was refused by the live per-cylinder census for holding a prefab not on CLEARABLE, and the blocker's POSITION is not obtainable: MEASURED, `objects_count id=*` reports those prefabs reproducibly and position-consistently (2 Pickable_Mushroom_yellow at r 9.68 m and 0 at r 7.35 m on S8, so they lie in that annulus) while `findObjects -prefab P -near` returns ZERO for the same name at every y band from -128 to +140 m, which is also why the corridor census never saw them to plan around.  With no position there is no blocker-clear sub-disc to derive, so instead each object the parent would have removed is re-proposed as its own smaller cylinder -- a strict subset of the parent, centred on the object so it always reaches it -- and the SAME live census that refused the parent decides each one.  Nothing is narrowed silently: a candidate is either censused clean and sent, or censused blocked and recorded with what blocked it.  THE LOCATION GATE IS INHERITED RATHER THAN RE-ASKED, and it is sound because the candidate is a SUBSET: `footprint_clear` and the non-destructive distance rule both hold for every point of the parent disc, so they hold for every point of a disc contained in it, and the wire names FEWER prefabs than the parent's -- all of them on CLEARABLE, so the budget cannot change from non-destructive to destructive.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.
meta.split_why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

params.method: MEASURED -- the per-cylinder disposition of THIS clearing pass, appended at the end of the same session that sent the removals: the plan's blocked-tile skips, the location gate's per-cylinder skips, the skips this call's own immediately-prior live census forced, the blocker-clear sub-discs actually sent with the derived parent disc each one is a subset of, and every object left inside the derived clearing width named by prefab + world position with the blocker that binds it.

MEASURED. (1) DISPOSITION off roads/applied.py's live union for the two segments re-cleared in this pass, over a FRESH live per-cell census taken after the removals: T4 82 -> 20 in width (buried 29 -> 9, floating 21 -> 2, worst burial -3.255 -> -2.945 m, worst float 3.217 -> 0.498 m) and S8 33 -> 1 (buried 16 -> 1, floating 9 -> 0, worst burial -1.528 -> -1.035 m). (2) THE `reach` EXIT OF `ribbon.stamp`'s BATTER RAY WALK WAS DEAD CODE: it was gated on `lat - edge > batter_m` while the member list is built from `LAT <= edge + batter_m`, the same bound, so no member could satisfy it -- MEASURED, `reach` occurred ZERO times across twelve battered segments while `lattice_end`, which is the ray falling out of its own member list with NO clip, NO residual and nothing for `edge_step_census` to consult, occurred 1 to 90 times per segment. Resolved into two recorded causes: `reach` when the outermost member sits within one lattice diagonal of the cap (the reach really is spent and the residual is a wall, now in `walls_left_by_cause`), and `bin_exhausted` when it sits further in (the station bin ran out of samples because `int(round(arc))` scatters a diagonal transect across adjacent stations; recorded in `ray_skip_at`). T8 4 of 9 termination reversals unaccounted -> 0 of 9, T13 1 -> 0, W5 1 -> 0, and the smooth baselines reproduce EXACTLY (T12 p50 0.71 / p95 2.12 / 0, T9 p50 0.00 / p95 1.41 / 0), which is what proves the change is recording only. (3) THE MARCHED REMOVAL-DISC COVER HAD A HOLE: the covering argument `(s/2)^2 + h^2 <= R^2` is plane geometry about a STRAIGHT strip and the step is marched along ARC, so a bend tighter than one step walks past the outside of it -- MEASURED on T4, 11 objects INSIDE their own station's derived clearing width and outside EVERY derived disc, worst 4.84 m short, at the node-328 hairpin where the march stepped 16.3 m of arc across the apex. `clear.cover_gaps` now tests the census's OWN predicate on a half-metre lattice and adds centreline discs until nothing in the strip is uncovered: T4 112 -> 143 discs, uncovered in-width objects 15 -> 5, and all 5 remaining have a BRIDGED nearest station, which writes no terrain. params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED and READ-ONLY. `clear.plan_removals` and `clear.location_gate` re-run OFFLINE over a census taken minutes ago, per object still standing inside this segment's DERIVED clearing width, to answer the operator's actual question -- why is THIS one still here. Nothing was removed and no terrain was written by this record. It is a PRESENT-TENSE verdict about the world as it stands, not a reconstruction of what an earlier clearing pass decided: those passes built their skip detail and discarded it, and MEASURED, 78 of 109 objects still standing network-wide had no reason anywhere in the chain before this pass. `REACHABLE_NOT_CLEARED` is recorded as WORK NOT DONE rather than as a reason.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh.
