params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T10_wtspawn_wtsouth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.name: road_T13_temple_harboursouth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.
meta.split_why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: the segment's own design grade

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

MEASURED, and the instruments are named per claim. (1) CLEARING. Nine segments cleared against the DERIVED clearing width (carriageway + shoulder + that station's own batter run + the 1 m terrain spread, over-reached by 0.35): T5 69 -> 10 in width, T1 18 -> 1, T10 11 -> 0, S7 15 -> 6, W5 9 -> 2, T8 5 -> 0, T9 3 -> 0, T13 7 -> 4, W10 4 -> 2. 81 objects_clear records, seqs 1818-1989; 148 objects by each cylinder's own immediately-prior live census (`deleted_live_count`), 149 positions listed, and the one difference is seq 1978 where the corridor census listed 3 candidates of the named prefabs and the live census counted 2 -- the extra position was already gone. Every removal names prefab + world position as the DURABLE KEY. (2) BATTER. Ten repair builds, each naming the terrain_write it repairs and carrying its measured before-state: T5 (repair_of 1378), S8 (1428), T8 (1197 then 1869), T13 (1579 then 1873), W5 (1535 then 1878), T10 (1050), S7 (1482), W10 (1549), T1 (1666), T9 (1300). zone_ctrl 1-of-1 in every zone of every write, 0 samples past the +/-8 m apply clamp, 0 below c_WaterLevel 30.0. (3) THE LOCUS TEST, which is the acceptance instrument for the operator's 'blocky on gradients': SMOOTH on all ten, with ZERO unaccounted reversals -- T8 was 4 of 9 unaccounted before the dead-`reach`-exit fix and is 0 of 9 now, T13 1 -> 0, W5 1 -> 0. (4) THE CLOSING NUMBER, off roads/applied.py's live union and this ledger, never off a run's own output, and DEDUPLICATED by prefab + world position because two segments' derived widths overlap: 50 unique objects inside a derived clearing width (52 census rows; the Beech_small1/RaspberryBush pair at (-327.4,-200.4) is claimed by BOTH W10 and W5 and is counted once), 21 buried worst -3.441 m, 11 floating worst 2.542 m, 18 flush. Was 268 (79/59/130). (5) THE REASON CLAIM, CHECKED OBJECT BY OBJECT rather than relayed: before this pass 31 of 109 carried a reason and NOTHING was recorded for nine of the fifteen built segments -- the claim 'every remaining object is recorded with its skip reason' was false by a factor of three and a half, twice. It is now TRUE and verified per object: 50 of 50, as blocked_by a non-clearable piece inside the 1 m standoff with its distance (16), a cylinder_skip naming the blockers (10), the plan's own left_standing (21), gate_shrink naming the location that narrowed the disc and the radius it took (2), and one NO_SENDABLE_DISC with its geometry. (6) A SHRINK IS SILENT was found a fourth time, in my own audit instrument: `location_gate` shrinks `cylinders_clear` IN PLACE, so reading the post-gate discs reported the W10/W5 pair as 'no sendable disc' when the truth is that a 14.64 m derived disc DID reach them and the WoodHouse4 stand-off narrowed it to 10.79 and 8.70 m. The record now names the location and both radii. (7) THE CONSOLE SINK IS NOT THE DOCKER LOG. `docker logs` has been frozen since 23:09:37Z, and the console table stayed readable the whole pass because `terraform/console.py` reads supervisord's own captured stdout inside the container on a byte offset: `objects_count id=_ZoneCtrl pos=-280,216 max=64` answered Total: 4 / _ZoneCtrl: 4 in 4.9 s with the docker log dead. `host_sink_state` returned to `circular_wait` repeatedly under census load and `clear.sink_watch`'s host drain cleared it every time: that is a STANDING PROPERTY of this fleet with an automatic remedy, not an incident to re-diagnose.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

retry_of.why: ASK THE GUARD, DO NOT MODEL IT.  This cylinder's parent was refused by the live per-cylinder census for holding a prefab not on CLEARABLE, and the blocker's POSITION is not obtainable: MEASURED, `objects_count id=*` reports those prefabs reproducibly and position-consistently (2 Pickable_Mushroom_yellow at r 9.68 m and 0 at r 7.35 m on S8, so they lie in that annulus) while `findObjects -prefab P -near` returns ZERO for the same name at every y band from -128 to +140 m, which is also why the corridor census never saw them to plan around.  With no position there is no blocker-clear sub-disc to derive, so instead each object the parent would have removed is re-proposed as its own smaller cylinder -- a strict subset of the parent, centred on the object so it always reaches it -- and the SAME live census that refused the parent decides each one.  Nothing is narrowed silently: a candidate is either censused clean and sent, or censused blocked and recorded with what blocked it.  THE LOCATION GATE IS INHERITED RATHER THAN RE-ASKED, and it is sound because the candidate is a SUBSET: `footprint_clear` and the non-destructive distance rule both hold for every point of the parent disc, so they hold for every point of a disc contained in it, and the wire names FEWER prefabs than the parent's -- all of them on CLEARABLE, so the budget cannot change from non-destructive to destructive.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

params.method: MEASURED -- the per-cylinder disposition of THIS clearing pass, appended at the end of the same session that sent the removals: the plan's blocked-tile skips, the location gate's per-cylinder skips, the skips this call's own immediately-prior live census forced, the blocker-clear sub-discs actually sent with the derived parent disc each one is a subset of, and every object left inside the derived clearing width named by prefab + world position with the blocker that binds it.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

retry_of.why: ASK THE GUARD, DO NOT MODEL IT.  This cylinder's parent was refused by the live per-cylinder census for holding a prefab not on CLEARABLE, and the blocker's POSITION is not obtainable: MEASURED, `objects_count id=*` reports those prefabs reproducibly and position-consistently (2 Pickable_Mushroom_yellow at r 9.68 m and 0 at r 7.35 m on S8, so they lie in that annulus) while `findObjects -prefab P -near` returns ZERO for the same name at every y band from -128 to +140 m, which is also why the corridor census never saw them to plan around.  With no position there is no blocker-clear sub-disc to derive, so instead each object the parent would have removed is re-proposed as its own smaller cylinder -- a strict subset of the parent, centred on the object so it always reaches it -- and the SAME live census that refused the parent decides each one.  Nothing is narrowed silently: a candidate is either censused clean and sent, or censused blocked and recorded with what blocked it.  THE LOCATION GATE IS INHERITED RATHER THAN RE-ASKED, and it is sound because the candidate is a SUBSET: `footprint_clear` and the non-destructive distance rule both hold for every point of the parent disc, so they hold for every point of a disc contained in it, and the wire names FEWER prefabs than the parent's -- all of them on CLEARABLE, so the budget cannot change from non-destructive to destructive.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. params.text: dock-dockshore: a NEW waterfront structure. THE BEST-JUSTIFIED NEW WATERFRONT ON THIS WORLD, and the test is road access rather than water: TWO built trunk roads terminate here and there is nothing at the end of either. T5-temple-dockshore and T9-wttown-dockshore both end at the `dockshore` node (675.4, -85.6), whose own spec says 'early-dock / sandbox-harbour solved to water_dist_m 0.0. The ROAD stops on the shoreline; the pier is Crossings'' over-water structure' -- and Crossings never built one. MEASURED at 8 m: water fraction 0.820 in a 35 m disc, the HIGHEST of all 14 key places on this world; max depth 7.05 m; shelter 0.542. WHY 40 m AND NOT 24: crossings/plan.py::aim_seaward REFUSED a 24 m pier here at EVERY one of 72 bearings and at every head depth from 2.2 to 3.0 m -- the shelf is shallow and a short pier cannot reach water a boat floats in. Swept by length, 40 m is the shortest that the aimer accepts: root (691,-94), bearing 130, wet fraction 0.512 under the deck, head depth 4.33 m. 48 m would reach 6.05 m and is not needed, because 4.33 m already clears the deepest-draught vessel in the world (CargoShip, 2.0 m) by 1.33 m. The refusal is the measurement: a 24 m boathouse here would have been scenery.

result.objects_count_reply: objects_count printed no Total line; console said ['Error: Entity id mm_large_wall not recognized.']. An empty answer is not a zero -- that is how a removal gets aimed at nothing -- so this is a stop, not a 0.

params.method: MEASURED from the 4,872-prefab modded PieceGeometry dump, WITH THE LIMIT STATED: the JOINT PITCH is solid, both fb_bridge_01 and fb_bridge_02 span 18.614 m on their length axis, identically, so they tile at 18.614 m and a 96 m corridor needs 6 pieces (96/18.614 = 5.16). The DECK HEIGHT ABOVE PIVOT IS NOT DERIVABLE FROM THIS INSTRUMENT and must not be taken from these numbers: the only geometry either prefab carries for its deck is a `mesh`/`mesh_render` AABB (7.809 m for _01, 4.000 m for _02) which spans the whole ARCH, and its four real box colliders are 0.483 x 0.25 m railing posts, not a deck slab. Reading 7.809 as a walking height is the same mesh-AABB error that put tower beacons 5.173 m in the air and oversized every slip by 60%. Getting the true deck height needs a raycast or a player standing on the placed piece, neither of which RCON can do

meta.why: counts the two probes that DID place; mm_large_wall is deliberately NOT counted, because its absence IS the result

params.text: lh-north: RETIRING THE HALF-BUILT BODY AND RE-PLACING IT WHOLE, in one token hold. spawn_plan seq 2164 timed out part way through its 28 batches -- the game's stdout pipe backed up, pid 120208 sat in pipe_write, the main thread stopped answering RCON, and 272 of 1255 pieces were standing when the sink was drained FROM THE HOST with no SIGKILL. That record's expect is a full-body count at tolerance 0, so it is NOT re-emitted: re-sending it would double the 272 and fail its own postcondition on 1527. Instead: an unscoped live census, a retire per standing prefab aimed at a MEASURED cube, the site counted EMPTY, and then the body placed as 20 records of 64 pieces with the sink measured from the host and the main thread probed before every one. No terrain is written -- the pad from seq 2163 stands, and a second write to its zones would destroy the first one's terrain. Precedent: ledger seq 73.

lh-north: ANNOTATING seq 2269 and 2270 (my own, this chain). Those two spawn_plan records landed batches 1 and 2 of 20, and then the PROCESS RUNNING THE PASS WAS KILLED by its harness -- not the game, not the sink: the host /proc read showed supervisord in do_poll and syslogd in __skb_wait_for_more_packets, i.e. healthy, and RCON answered in 35 ms afterwards. seq 2270's wire DID go out in full: a live star count inside the 7.28 m radius reads 128, and the plan's first 128 lines hold exactly stone_floor_2x2 34, stone_stair 1, stone_wall_1x1 26, stone_wall_2x1 59, wood_pole 1, wood_stair 1, woodiron_pole 6 -- which is what the world holds, prefab for prefab. So neither record is re-sent and neither is retired. This pass RESUMES by a PER-PIECE diff: every one of the 1255 plan lines is matched against the live census by prefab and world position, and only the lines with nothing standing at them are sent, against a baseline measured live. A resume driven by which records were appended would have been a guess, because an appended record cannot say whether its own wire reached the world.

params.method: MEASURED from the HOST's /proc: wchan of the container's supervisord and syslogd plus supervisord's read ends of syslogd's stdout pipes, matched by pipe inode. No docker exec, which is the call that blocks while the sink is stalled and made the in-container probe report fds_lost for a drainable wait.

params.method: MEASURED live at the FINISHED sibling that carries the same blueprint: a scoped count of stone_wall_1x1 and the star count inside the same 7.28 m radius. This decides whether lh-north's missing stone_wall_1x1 are a prefab that does not spawn or commands the wedged wire never sent.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY. Disjoint 16 m cells on the global 16 m lattice; one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` per cell at five y levels (-32,-16,0,+16,+32); a reply over 18 rows re-asked as eight TILING sub-boxes so nothing approaches the client's 4096-byte buffer. Deduplicated by prefab + WORLD POSITION because ZDO ids are reassigned on world load.

value.durable_key: prefab + WORLD POSITION; ZDO ids are reassigned on world load

params.method: MEASURED per piece: every plan line's target position matched against the live census by prefab and by max axis offset within 0.15 m, each live piece claimable once. The remainder is the set of lines with no piece standing at them, so a resume can neither duplicate a placed piece nor skip a missing one. ZDO ids are not used: they are reassigned on world load.

params.text: lh-north: RETIRING THE HALF-BUILT BODY AND RE-PLACING IT WHOLE, in one token hold. spawn_plan seq 2164 timed out part way through its 28 batches -- the game's stdout pipe backed up, pid 120208 sat in pipe_write, the main thread stopped answering RCON, and 272 of 1255 pieces were standing when the sink was drained FROM THE HOST with no SIGKILL. That record's expect is a full-body count at tolerance 0, so it is NOT re-emitted: re-sending it would double the 272 and fail its own postcondition on 1527. Instead: an unscoped live census, a retire per standing prefab aimed at a MEASURED cube, the site counted EMPTY, and then the body placed as 20 records of 64 pieces with the sink measured from the host and the main thread probed before every one. No terrain is written -- the pad from seq 2163 stands, and a second write to its zones would destroy the first one's terrain. Precedent: ledger seq 73.

lh-north: ANNOTATING seq 2401 AND CUTTING THE DIFF OVER TO ONE PROBE PER PIECE. seq 2401's postcondition failed and the record stands: it deleted both copies of a duplicated wood_pole_log_4 correctly and then asserted the prefab ABSENT inside a 0.3 m disc, which is FALSE while the second wood_pole_log_4 of that same XZ column stands 4 m above it at y 75.98. objects_count is an XZ CYLINDER and therefore y-blind, and this body stacks the same prefab above itself (wood_pole_log_4 at 71.98 and 75.98, wood_roof at 76.98 and 79.98). The delete cube was right -- the cube metric puts that neighbour 4 m away -- the CHECK was wrong. Dedupe postconditions are now exact column counts: the delete asserts the plan's own number of that prefab in the disc MINUS ONE, the re-place asserts it back. Second correction, and it is the bigger one: the per-piece diff no longer runs off the 16 m box census at all. That census twice called standing pieces missing -- once from the silent y window, once with a residual 3-piece shortfall and no unlisted box to show for it -- and re-sending a standing piece is what doubles a body. The diff is now ONE PROBE PER PLANNED PIECE: findObjects -prefab P -near x y z h over a cube of half h = half that position's own measured distance to the nearest same-prefab piece (0.133 to 0.300 m across all 1255, none refused), so every probe has exactly one possible answer. The box census is kept only for what it is good at: foreign objects and their distance.

params.method: MEASURED from the HOST's /proc: wchan of the container's supervisord and syslogd plus supervisord's read ends of syslogd's stdout pipes, matched by pipe inode. No docker exec, which is the call that blocks while the sink is stalled and made the in-container probe report fds_lost for a drainable wait.

gate.method: HOST-side /proc read via sudo: wchan of the container's supervisord and syslogd (host pids from `docker top`), and supervisord's read ends of syslogd's stdout/stderr pipes matched by pipe inode. No `docker exec`, which is the call that blocks when the sink is stalled and makes the in-container probe report `fds_lost` spuriously.

params.method: MEASURED live at the FINISHED sibling that carries the same blueprint: a scoped count of stone_wall_1x1 and the star count inside the same 7.28 m radius. This decides whether lh-north's missing stone_wall_1x1 are a prefab that does not spawn or commands the wedged wire never sent.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY. Disjoint 16 m cells on the global 16 m lattice; one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` per cell at each requested y level, the levels 16 m apart so the 8 m half-boxes TILE in y and the window is reported rather than assumed; a reply over 18 rows re-asked as eight TILING sub-boxes so nothing approaches the client's 4096-byte buffer. One row per prefab + WORLD POSITION because ZDO ids are reassigned on world load, with `at_position` counting the distinct ZDOs sharing that position within this census.

value.durable_key: prefab + WORLD POSITION; ZDO ids are reassigned on world load

params.method: MEASURED one probe per planned piece: `findObjects -prefab P -near x y z h -detailed` over a CUBE of half h = half this position's own measured distance to the nearest other piece of the same prefab, capped at 0.30 m. Every probe therefore has exactly one possible answer -- 0 means the piece is not there, 1 means it is, more than 1 is a duplicate -- which a 16 m box census of a 48 m tower cannot promise, and twice did not deliver. The reply comes over the SOCKET, so 1,255 probes cost round trips and no console-sink pressure; the sink is measured from the host every 60 probes anyway.

mechanism.CORRECTION: the /srv record this replaces named network/plan.py:262-264. WRONG FILE. That planner did not light this network: the placing wire is `spawn_object piece_groundtorch ... data=<everburning payload>` under role `road_lighting`, emitted by roads/lamps.py as actor Lampposts.
mechanism.chain_break_disarms_the_minimum: ::site sets `last_s = None` when a window holds nothing legal. `_biome_allows` then takes its `last_s is None` branch, which tests ONLY `s - base_s <= pol['max_m']` -- there is no minimum at all. So the first lamp after a chain break has its spacing unchecked against the lamp before the break. This is a code-exact fourth mechanism and it was not in the brief.
mechanism.fence_post: the brief's hypothesis, TESTED AND REFUTED as stated: lamps are NOT doubled at s=0/s=L. 0 of 138 markers sit within 12 m of any segment's s=0 and only 2 within 12 m of any s=L; the first lamp on a segment starts between 19 m and 295 m in. mechanism.population_considered: `last_s` ONLY -- the previous lamp in THIS call's own greedy chain on THIS segment. `last_s` is a local of `site()` initialised to None per segment, so the minimum spacing is enforced against exactly one lamp and the function never reads the world. It is therefore blind to (a) lamps on any other segment, (b) lamps already standing from an earlier run, and (c) lamps placed by anything that is not the lighting pass, such as the lighthouse and harbour bodies.
mechanism.repeat_runs: CONFIRMED and the largest single contributor, 11 of 34 pairs. The 138 markers fall into 15 ZDO-id families; 11 sub-30 m pairs span families thousands of ids apart (4.019 m at |did| 1943, 8.302 m at 1966, 13.020 m at 1825). params.text: PortalTriage TAKING the write token at tools/jumpstart/ledger/runs/Ulfsland/ledger.jsonl sha256 84bdffaf6083462f052e7cdd7acbe7285217a0c1789b371a878d20ed5e530dea (2509 lines, head seq 2504 save LampSpacing). WORLD BACKED UP FIRST: /media/big4/projects/game/valheim/world_backups/world-Ulfsland-PortalTriage-pre-retag-2026-09-18_01-02-36.tgz, 5325128 B, tar tzf verified 27 real members including _main.311.db2. On taking the token ledger.lock's TEXT read 'pid 4188001 actor FerryPair op save since 2026-09-18T03:52:19Z' and pid 4188001 was DEAD; the file was NOT unlinked. MEASURED (LampSpacing, writer.py:936-957): the real mutual exclusion is an fcntl flock held by the open file description, which the kernel releases on process exit, so the text is a human breadcrumb that _append_raw rewrites on every append and is never read as authority. A dead pid in a lock file is grounds to investigate, not authority to clear, and unlinking is the one act that CAN break exclusion for a live holder. TONIGHT'S STRUCTURAL DEFECT, recorded because it cost four agents an hour: flock is PER-INODE, and a second checkout at /srv/valheim-portal carried a FORKED ledger with its own lock. Two locks, two pids, one live world, ZERO mutual exclusion -- while every agent followed the token protocol correctly. Identical prefix to line 1737, then divergence. Proven canonical by the WORLD: /media projects to 20 live tags / 40 ends, matching the 59 portal_wood located individually; /srv projects to 18 and does not know x-north or x-vestvik exist, both of which are standing. A token announcement must carry the absolute path AND its hash or it is unfalsifiable.

params.method: MEASURED live, every one of the 59 portal_wood in the world located individually and its tag read off the ZDO. objects_count id=portal_wood = Total: 59, twice. Hall occupancy read as one 30 m cube (header 20, 20 rows). Bay capacity from portal_hall.bays(), which returns 24 and raises at 26. Each of the 20 tags probed at its ledger far-end coordinate at r=12; every tag returned exactly one site end, giving 20 tags x 2 ends. Blanks localised by an objects_count quadtree on COUNT (cheap, XZ cylinder, no y trap) then listed with bounded findObjects.
params.tool: findObjects -prefab portal_wood -near <x> <y> <z> <r> -detailed (native ValheimRcon verb) + objects_count id=portal_wood

value.instrument_defect_I_committed: my own first castle probe returned ZERO because I centred a cube at y=60 while the castle's 15-arch ring stands at y=110.95. findObjects -near is a CUBE; a y window chosen for the ground is blind to a hilltop. Same class as the documented 48 m tower miss.

Origin is ledger seq 545 observe, whose own method reads 'every portal_wood inside 30 m of the castle and 40 m of each village centre' -- a fixed radius about named centres, which is not a world census. The two missed are in Stenvik at (554.71,49.87,909.43), 58.9 m from the Stenvik centre and OUTSIDE the 40 m disc, and (522.71,46.20,890.93) at 30.5 m but at y 46-50 against a castle-height y window.
reconciliation.18: portal_hall.py's MOVE COUNT, i.e. bays(need=18) -- the number REQUESTED. Not capacity (24) and not occupancy (20). x-north and x-vestvik were added after it ran.
reconciliation.20_two_ended: the LEDGER projection (59 portal records minus retirements). The ONLY one of the four that agrees with live measurement -- confirmed end by end, not assumed.
reconciliation.33/22/11pairs/11blank: an EARLIER WORLD STATE, superseded. The world now holds 59 portal_wood; that snapshot predates the castle, Sudrberg, Vestvik and Stenvik bodies.

value.wedge_I_caused: an adaptive subdividing findObjects sweep whose top-level replies sat at the 4050 B truncation point took the main thread and the sink to circular_wait after ~30 calls, and a peer's connect timed out on it. findObjects iterates EVERY ZDO per call regardless of filter, so cost is per-call while the hazard is per-reply-byte. Repaired from the HOST with drain_log_sink_host: released in 1.2 s, game untouched, no restart.

params.method: MEASURED live: every board's text read off its ZDO, its own arch resolved through portal_hall.DISPLAY, and Euclidean distance compared board->own arch vs board->nearest arch.

value.anonymous_arches: the 4 off-lattice INNER arches (x-harbour, x-ferry-e, x-north, x-vestvik) have NO board at all -- anonymous arches standing on the walking floor in the middle of a hub, which is the operator's original 'portals spread throughout the woods' complaint in a new form
value.fix: place the board along the arch's FACING axis instead -- step = (sin yaw, cos yaw), which in this hall is the inward radial -- reusing the same fixtures.fixture_box walk so clearance is still solved and not declared. value.root_cause: network/waypoints.py::portal_guidepost walks the post along the arch's WIDTH axis -- step = (cos yaw, -sin yaw), perpendicular to facing. In a 22.5 deg-spaced arcade whose bays are 5.39 m apart that axis points AT THE NEIGHBOURING BAY. The function is correct for a lone arch on open ground, which is what it was solved and verified against; it was never wrong about clearance, it is wrong about ATTRIBUTION in a ring.

value.why_it_matters: anyone who 'corrects' a spawn_object wire to x,z,y on the strength of the objects_count result lands every piece with X and Z swapped, AND IT PASSES A NAIVE COUNT CHECK, because a transposed position is still a position. Two agents hit this tonight from opposite directions.

meta.why: The operator reported the hub 'fairly full of too many portals in the middle area' and asked for portals to the main NORTHERN areas, leaving out ends such as ferry landings. MEASURED before this pass: 20 arches held portals in the hall (capacity 24), all 20 tagged, 0 blank in the hall, and 19 blank-tag portal_wood stood ELSEWHERE forming ONE uniform random destination pool whose worst-case jump is 6201 m. This pass reduces the hall to 13 live tags in the 15-bay outer arcade, empties all 9 inner bays, holds bays 5 and 6 EMPTY for the northern trunk road, and removes every blank-tag portal in the world.

params.method: MEASURED, then ranked by travel VALUE rather than existence. Every input is measured: straight-line distance from the hall; ROAD distance over the 15 road segments actually BUILT (read out of this chain's own zones_generate/terrain_write/objects_clear names, NOT the spec's full edge list); piece counts from each body's own expect.prefab_count; hall bay geometry from portal_hall.bays(). The WEIGHTING of those measurements -- destination vs waypoint vs transit-only, and the operator's NORTH preference -- is judgement applied to measured inputs and is labelled as such rather than dressed as a measurement.
params.tool: tools/jumpstart/settlements/portal_hall.py bays() + the built-road graph out of the canonical ledger

value.blanks_retired_not_purposed: all 19. Every site hosting one already keeps a tagged arch to the hall (castle, Stenvik, Vestvik, Sudrberg), so nothing loses access. Purposing the castle's 15-arch ring would have built a SECOND HUB -- the exact sprawl this pass removes.

dropped_7_with_reasons.u-treenear: LOWEST VALUE: a 23-piece treehouse platform at 556 m -- the SHORTEST trip of all 20 tags. An arch that saves 556 m is the weakest use of a bay in a hall whose own front door is 310 m from the temple.
dropped_7_with_reasons.u-wtsouth: WAYPOINT + WALKABLE: 43-piece lookout, 967 m by built road (T1/T12/T10). A lookout is a thing you look FROM on the way past, not a destination.
dropped_7_with_reasons.u-wtspawn: WAYPOINT + WALKABLE: a 43-piece lookout 515 m from the hall by built road (T1+T12), beside the spawn the player already stands at. Shortest-value arch in the set.
dropped_7_with_reasons.u-wttown: WAYPOINT + COVERED: 43-piece lookout, walkable 1892 m by built road, and 384 m from Stenvik, which keeps its arch.
dropped_7_with_reasons.x-ferry-e: FERRY LANDING, named by the operator as a drop. ferry-terminal-eastisle is a transit point between two shores; 48 pieces, no bed, nothing to arrive at.
dropped_7_with_reasons.x-harbour: TRANSIT-ONLY: a CargoShip berth at harbour-temple-south, and road-walkable 583 m from the hall on T13. A berth is where you change from land to sea, not a place to arrive at.
dropped_7_with_reasons.x-vestvik: TRANSIT-ONLY + COVERED: harbour-vestvik is Vestvik's harbour, 253 m from Vestvik village, which keeps its own arch. A harbour serving a portalled destination does not need a second arch.

value.middle_emptied_why: the operator's words were 'fairly full of too many portals in the middle area'. MEASURED: 5 arches stood in the inner ring at r 6-9 m on the hall's walking floor and 4 of them had NO guidepost at all. Every kept arch now stands in the 15-bay outer arcade.
value.reserved_why: bays 5 and 6 held EMPTY for TrunkNorth's north-staging (-192,2698) and north-terminus (measured frontier -1164,7814, still moving). NO placeholder portal: a reserved bay carrying a blank tag would be indistinguishable from the defect being removed and would join the random pool. An empty labelled bay is a complete, honest end state.

meta.why: a postcondition that measures a different shape from the command it verifies will pass until the day it does not

params.text: MY OWN DEFECT, recorded at the moment it fired rather than after it was tidied. seq 2544 is a retire of wood_pole_log 39888:1 at (-275.34, 40.85, 201.66) whose postcondition FAILED with absent[wood_pole_log] want 0 got 1. THE DELETE WAS CORRECT AND THE OBJECT IS GONE -- re-measured immediately afterwards, findObjects -prefab wood_pole_log -near -275.34 40.85 201.66 4 returns only 43348:1 and 43350:1, both of which are OTHER posts still standing and both later targets in this same pass. THE CHECK WAS WRONG, not the world. CAUSE, and it is a geometry mismatch inside one toolchain: `deleteObjects -near x y z r` is a 3-D CUBE, while `expect: {absent: [{pos:[x,z], max:r}]}` is an XZ DISC THAT IGNORES Y. Post 43350:1 lies 1.092 m from the target in XZ but 2.90 m below it in Y, so the cube rightly spared it and the disc rightly counted it. I had proved radius safety with a 3-D Chebyshev separation (worst 3.270 m over the portals) and that proof does not apply to the postcondition's shape -- I proved the wrong thing and it passed 33 times before it failed, which is the dangerous kind. FIX: radii are now solved from the LIVE XZ nearest-neighbour per target, radius = max(0.25, min(1.2, 0.45 * nn_xz)); MEASURED worst nn_xz over the 36 signage targets is 1.092 m, giving radii 0.49-1.20 m. seq 2544 is left standing as the failed record it is and this note is its cause; the target is re-emitted under a correct radius. GENERAL RULE for this tree: before trusting a radius, state the SHAPE of every check that radius feeds -- cube for findObjects/deleteObjects -near, XZ cylinder for objects_count pos=/max= and for expect.absent.

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: the segment's own design grade

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.
