the harbour is DREDGED rather than berth-hunted: the shallowest sample under a CargoShip's own hull passing the gate MEASURED 2.890 m against 3.000 m required, so the gate refused the deepest hull the basin could otherwise take

params.datum: a DREDGE, not a pad: every delta is min(applied, 24) - generated at that sample, against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68), so the write can only ever DEEPEN. A positive delta is the operation MEASURED to remove water and this write is structurally incapable of one.

fixture_narrowings.why: a structure inside the stand-off. It is recorded rather than moved because the stand-off exists to stop a TERRAIN WRITE cutting the ground out from under a LocationProxy, and this fixture writes none. The dredge's own stand-off is measured separately over the cut samples.

location_check.method: MEASURED: every LIVE LocationProxy within reach of this site, read over RCON with bounded `findObjects -prefab LocationProxy -near x 30 z r`, and every fixture of this design tested against the nearest one. THE DREDGE'S OWN verdict is measured over EVERY CUT SAMPLE against every marker, because the cut is an area and a check at its centre is a check of its centre. Fixture checks that come in inside the stand-off are listed under `fixture_narrowings` with their distances; they write no terrain, and a structure cannot drain anything.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.text: PortalTriage TAKING the token at sha256 5fca97fa623148661f68f99e49fcceb30832afc889ea1de32061461842e4ae42 (2880 records, head seq 2875 save RoadNorthLand), re-hashed with my own Ledger.open immediately before record 1. u-nterm is placed because the northern trunk road REACHED its terminus: 11,453.8 m of continuous walkable road, all 16 channel spans decked, northernmost walkable z +7,730.0. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SPEC, both measured. (1) 'lit end to end, 242 lamps' is CORRIDOR-SCOPED and not true of the arrival point: objects_count id=* at (-846,7730) r=20 m returns Total 19 of which ZERO are built pieces -- 1 _TerrainCompiler, 1 _ZoneCtrl, 4 firs, 11 rocks, 2 fungus -- and at r=40 m exactly ONE piece_groundtorch, 26.6 m away at (-872.41, 7733.55). So the original binding objection stands on its facts: nothing is built at the terminus, no bed, no shelter, Mountain. The arch is placed anyway because the SUBJECT changed, not the rule: the destination is the terminus of an 11.45 km built road whose northern half is unusable while its far end sits behind a 7.5 km walk, and at 11,453.8 m this is 5x the longest walk any kept arch spares (u-stenvik, 2,256 m by road). The rule was never 'there must be a bed' -- 43-piece watchtowers and 23-piece treehouses were kept, and ends were dropped for being WALKABLE, not unfurnished. A shelter with a bed and a campfire at the terminus is the follow-up that makes this a proper destination and it is named here rather than implied to be done. transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.
meta.split_why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

params.method: MEASURED -- the per-cylinder disposition of THIS clearing pass, appended at the end of the same session that sent the removals: the plan's blocked-tile skips, the location gate's per-cylinder skips, the skips this call's own immediately-prior live census forced, the blocker-clear sub-discs actually sent with the derived parent disc each one is a subset of, and every object left inside the derived clearing width named by prefab + world position with the blocker that binds it.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.
meta.split_why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.after: objects_count ids="<the same named prefab list>" ignore="_*" total=0 tolerance=0

proof_both_directions.must_still_refuse: the check is strictly sharper for the command's own promise - if any named prefab survived the removal it is counted and the record fails, where the old `*` check could have been satisfied only by an empty cylinder and so conflated 'my removal worked' with 'nothing is here'
proof_both_directions.now_passes: the seq 3002 cylinder: 0 of the 11 named prefabs remain, so the rescoped check answers 0 and passes, with the deer and the gull still standing in it

params.method: MEASURED live immediately after the failure, with the same instrument the check uses: `objects_count` over the 11 named ids answered 0, and `objects_count id=*` over the identical cylinder answered 2, both animals

value.cause: `settlements/build.py::scoped_clear` sends `objects_remove id=<11 named prefabs>` - deliberately named rather than `id=*`, because a star also deletes whatever arrives between the measurement and the removal - but its postcondition asked `objects_count id=* total=0`. The command promises 'these named prefabs are gone'; the check demanded 'this cylinder is empty of everything', which no removal can make true of a world with wildlife in it.
value.class: The command and its postcondition are two statements of one question, and they were not reconciled. Same family as seq 2988 (square expectation, disc measurement) and seq 2690 (cube expectation, cylinder measurement); this one differs about WHAT is being counted rather than about where.
value.fix: The expectation is now scoped to the same id list the wire carries: `objects_count id=<the same 11 prefabs> total=0`. That is also STRICTLY SHARPER than the old check for what the command did - it can no longer pass because the cylinder happens to be empty of something nobody removed.

measured_after_the_failure.reading: every prefab the command named is gone; the only two objects in the cylinder are a deer and a gull that walked and flew in between the removal and the count

value.not_repaired: Nothing removed, nothing re-sent. The stage resumes from unit 1, whose re-measured cylinder now holds no clearable object, so its clearing will correctly emit a skip rather than an empty removal.
value.note: `cylinder_verdict` in harbour_b.py already classifies creatures as MOBILE and explicitly does not count them as blocking, so the module's PRE-clear gate had this right and only the POST-clear check forgot.
value.verdict: THE REMOVAL WAS COMPLETE. THE CHECK ASKED A DIFFERENT QUESTION.
value.why_it_is_a_gate_with_no_open_position: Meadows spawns deer and gulls continuously. A 12.35 m cylinder in open Meadows cannot be held empty, so this check's pass depended on no animal wandering through during the round trip. It passed 51 times on this chain by luck of timing and failed the 52nd, one record into a 14-terrace stage.

params.what: seq 3002's failed postcondition, diagnosed: the clearing was complete and its check demanded an empty cylinder in a biome that spawns wildlife; `scoped_clear`'s postcondition is rescoped to the ids the command actually removes

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp
meta.why_terraced: MEASURED over 8,075 lattice centres at harbour B: not one 16, 20 or 24 m pad is flat to 0.6 m, so seating a body on the applied surface at the footprint median would stand a 20 m hall with up to 4.7 m of hillside through its floor

params.datum: pad target_y 32.52 m; deltas against the heightmap surface at 1 m (seed Pirate68). `heightmap` is HeightmapBuilder's per-zone corner-biome blend -- the ground the engine draws and the one ApplyToHeightmap adds the delta to -- NOT WorldGenerator.GetHeight, which differs by up to 8.807 m on this seed and is what left wt-peak's watchtower in the air

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

meta.union: the blob is the UNION of everything each zone keeps: this pad's rectangle re-valued, every other modified sample carried forward VERBATIM from the ledger's own blobs composed in FILE ORDER. merged_from names every prior write in each zone.
meta.why: sudrberg-keep was levelled against WorldGenerator.GetHeight, so the ground the engine renders under it is (heightmap - worldgen) away from 121.84 and everything seated on the pad is off by that amount. The pad rectangle is re-valued against the heightmap surface and NOTHING MOVES. The alternative -- move the datum and every body with it -- is what wt-peak needed because its raise costs 8.425 m against the +/-8 m clamp; here it costs 4.746 m and is legal, so no object is touched.

params.datum: target_y 121.84 m UNCHANGED from seq 752 -- this record changes only the surface the deltas are measured against, from WorldGenerator.GetHeight to HeightmapBuilder::Build, which is the ground the engine DRAWS and the one ApplyToHeightmap adds the delta to. Keeping target_y is what makes this repair move NO OBJECT: everything on this pad was seated at 121.84 and lands on it again.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.text: seq 2909 FAILED FOR THE INSTRUMENT, NOT FOR THE MOUNT. That record is the first lintel test: one `sign` at (-278.9786, 40.5, 202.2351), dy 3.4 above the u-wtpeak arch, no post. Its postcondition came back prefab_count[sign] want 1 got 0 and a reader would take that as 'an unsupported sign at dy 3.4 does not hold'. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF THAT. Recorded by APPEND because the chain is never edited, and recorded at all because a retracted conclusion left standing in the record is inherited as fact.

meta.why: THE DEFECT, as the operator reported it: 'the signs in the portal hub are placed inside the archways which blocks the approach into the portal'. MEASURED over the 15 standing boards by /tmp/hallsigns.py against the live census: ALL 15 sit at LATERAL 0.0 mm on their own arch's facing ray -- that is exact and it is by construction, the previous solve walked each post OUTWARD ALONG THE FACING until it cleared the arch, which is the approach centreline by definition. ELEVEN of the 15 are inside the 2.94 x 3.00 x 2.00 m corridor volume (deepest penetration 0.700 m, and it is the POST that penetrates, not the board). The remaining FOUR -- the 45-degree bays u-lhwest, u-ulfsgard, u-vestvik, u-wteast -- stand 4.395 m out along the same ray and clear the corridor's far end by 0.150 m. They are moved too, and the 0.150 m is the reason rather than an exemption: a clearance smaller than the uncertainty in the corridor's own definition is not clearance, and it is on the ray a player walks in on. 'All 15 block the approach' was an overstatement; 'all 15 sit on the approach ray' is exact.

MEASURED over the 15 standing boards by /tmp/hallsigns.py against the live census: ALL 15 sit at LATERAL 0.0 mm on their own arch's facing ray -- that is exact and it is by construction, the previous solve walked each post OUTWARD ALONG THE FACING until it cleared the arch, which is the approach centreline by definition. ELEVEN of the 15 are inside the 2.94 x 3.00 x 2.00 m corridor volume (deepest penetration 0.700 m, and it is the POST that penetrates, not the board). The remaining FOUR -- the 45-degree bays u-lhwest, u-ulfsgard, u-vestvik, u-wteast -- stand 4.395 m out along the same ray and clear the corridor's far end by 0.150 m. They are moved too, and the 0.150 m is the reason rather than an exemption: a clearance smaller than the uncertainty in the corridor's own definition is not clearance, and it is on the ray a player walks in on. 'All 15 block the approach' was an overstatement; 'all 15 sit on the approach ray' is exact.

meta.cross_check: the generated surface was read TWICE -- a fresh PatchScan(SURFACE=heightmap) over both zones and the cached hmap_all.bin the diagnosis was made on -- and they agree to 0.000000 m over all 8,450 samples. The new blob's sample SET is identical to seq 545's in both zones (462 height, 462 paint); only the delta VALUES change, so the rectangle provably did not move.

flatten_guard.why: reached_this_write is the number of live flatten=FORBIDDEN records whose readable extent touches a zone this write claims. 0 means this guard measured NOTHING and its pass is vacuous -- safe, but not evidence. Non-zero with field_decoded true means every one of those records' pieces and discs was probed against this write's own TCData.

meta.merge_scope: scoped to WHAT THE BLOBS CLAIM: zones (22,24) and (23,24) are touched by exactly ONE terrain_write in the whole chain, seq 545, wt-peak's own, so the union carried forward is its own 462 samples and no road or neighbouring pad is in either blob. Asserted against the chain before the bytes were built, not assumed.
meta.why: wt-peak's pad was levelled to 102.310, a datum taken from WorldGenerator.GetHeight -- the height function of the POINT'S OWN biome.  The surface the engine DRAWS is HeightmapBuilder::Build, a blend over the ZONE'S FOUR CORNER biomes, and zone (22,24) has corners Meadows/Meadows/Meadows/Mountain over 2,736 of 4,225 Mountain interior samples, so it renders nearly pure Meadows at 93.885..99.427. The 212-piece tower, its portal and its guidepost therefore stand in 3.173..13.542 m of air.  Re-levelled to 96.656 (mid-range of the real ground over the pad's own 462 samples) and the whole body dropped 5.654 m with it. delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. meta.why: so the re-seating survives a restart AND so the applied surface can be re-read from the save's own TCData -- the verification instrument reads the save, not the ledger, precisely so a record whose write never landed cannot make the ground look repaired.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

flatten_guard.why: reached_this_write is the number of live flatten=FORBIDDEN records whose readable extent touches a zone this write claims. 0 means this guard measured NOTHING and its pass is vacuous -- safe, but not evidence. Non-zero with field_decoded true means every one of those records' pieces and discs was probed against this write's own TCData.

approach_reach_solve.why: no claim on this segment, so there is no approach to solve

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_R4_vestvik_harbour

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

unreachable.why: a non-clearable Pickable_ForestCryptRemains01 stands 1.56 m away, which leaves 0.56 m inside the 1 m standoff -- less than the 0.05 m minimum sendable cylinder, so no cylinder that reaches this object can avoid it

params.method: MEASURED -- the per-cylinder disposition of THIS clearing pass, appended at the end of the same session that sent the removals: the plan's blocked-tile skips, the location gate's per-cylinder skips, the skips this call's own immediately-prior live census forced, the blocker-clear sub-discs actually sent with the derived parent disc each one is a subset of, and every object left inside the derived clearing width named by prefab + world position with the blocker that binds it.

MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.durable_key: prefab + world position; the ZDO id is recorded alongside and is NOT durable across a world load
meta.policy: CLIP, never blanket, and SPLIT, never shrink: a cylinder may not hold any prefab off CLEARABLE, and a tile that does is covered by sub-discs that each stand wholly outside every blocker's standoff. A road crosses other people's property, so the road yields -- but it yields the blocker's neighbourhood, not the whole disc, and every object it still cannot reach is named with the blocker that binds it. That is the opposite of a settlement pad, which REFUSES rather than clips because a building cannot stand in half a clearing.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE. THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

THE DURABLE KEY IS PREFAB + POSITION, NOT THE ZDO ID -- MEASURED tonight by re-censusing T12 across a container restart: all 414 objects came back at byte-identical x, z and y with DIFFERENT ZDO ids (23163:1 -> 22958:1, 76580:1 -> 76288:1), so the ids are reassigned on world load and an id alone cannot identify an object to put back.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway
