walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height that pad's OWN write levelled it to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

value.grade_relaxed_why: THE PAD OWNS ITS OWN GROUND. Stations 0-4 lie inside (or within the carriageway half-width of) the portal-hall pad rectangle x[-298.7,-261.3] z[197.3,234.7] datum 37.100, so they take the datum: writer._pad_footprint_check refuses any re-emit that moves ground inside a pad footprint, and the old profile dived to 35.100 there, which is the 1.750 m trench MEASURED on the save at (-298,214)->(-299,214)->(-300,214). Holding the datum costs 8.0 m of the 26.0 m descent arc; the remaining 6.5 m to the S2 abutment level run (30.600, FIXED by the Crossings contract at (-316,230)) must then be carried over 18.0 m, which is grade 0.3616. MEASURED against the only limit that governs a walker, tan(38 deg) = 0.7813 per 1 m lattice edge (Character::c_MinSlideDegreesPlayer): 0.3616 is 46 % of it, and the road it replaces was IMPASSABLE - three over-limit mesh edges at 1.750, 1.750 and 1.000 m, which is why nothing could walk out of the hall's west door. The alternative that keeps 0.25 is 8.0 m more arc, i.e. a re-route or a raised abutment; both were refused as larger changes than the defect. Derived by roads/junction.py::pin_to_pad, applied by ::pinned_profile, and the emit was proved CLEAN (0 disputed samples change owner) by ::clean_order before it was written.
value.why: 30 m ramp from the portal hall down onto the S2 bridge deck. The hall stands 6.8 m above the abutment 30 m away, so no 12 % profile reaches it -- interval propagation PROVED 2 stations infeasible at 12 %. The measured requirement is 22 %, which is under the network's 25 % ceiling and less than a third of the 38 deg (78 %) angle at which Character::GetSlideAngle makes a player slide. A short bridge ramp is the right answer here; a 60 m switchback to save 10 % of grade over 30 m is worse for someone on foot.

meta.why: paint alpha is NOT honoured on a zone that has never been generated -- MEASURED, a paved_cleared pad in an ungenerated zone still planted 30+ vegetation ZDOs up to 7.68 m above it

census.waiver: annulus repair of a road already on the ground: the pad keep-out is now the samples the pad LEVELLED, not its declared rectangle+apron, and applied.owners_at no longer attributes zero-weight corners; profile UNCHANGED

flatten_guard.why: reached_this_write is the number of live flatten=FORBIDDEN records whose readable extent touches a zone this write claims. 0 means this guard measured NOTHING and its pass is vacuous -- safe, but not evidence. Non-zero with field_decoded true means every one of those records' pieces and discs was probed against this write's own TCData.

repair_before.instrument: roads/applied.py Applied.sample (live blob delta, per-sample AUTHORSHIP) + roads/ribbon.py zone_patches (the SEED bed); composed height = generated + delta, the way Heightmap composes the mesh
repair_before.population: the z=214 lattice row across the portal-hall apron, x -310..-291
repair_before.why: (-299,214) is the unwritten annulus sample: authored by road_S1_portalhub_brgs2 seq 417 at -1.578 m and never revisited, because applied.owners_at zero-weight corners made portal-hall#801 read as its owner and ribbon.refusal returned foreign. S1 plan holds 37.100 at the stations either side.

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: the segment's own design grade

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: the segment's own design grade

approach_reach_solve.why: the longest reach, inside the gradient tie band, whose rasterisation the +/-8 m apply clamp accepts -- asked of `stamp` per candidate, never predicted

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

approach_reach_solve.why: no claim on this segment, so there is no approach to solve

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T5_temple_dockshore

params.method: MEASURED: A* over a 1 m PatchScan field (rivers included) with the achievable surface clipped to +/-7 m of generated ground; profile fitted by exact interval propagation under the grade limit and the cut/fill box

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle. A GAP IS JUDGED SEPARATELY AND IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: `step_into_m` is the worst adjacent-station rise walking from the last written rim THROUGH the gap to the first written rim after it, against the same slide limit scaled by the two stations' own separation - which is the climb out of an unwritten notch, NOT `step_across_m`, the two rims measured against each other. A bridged run is exempt because the ribbon must not write terrain there and the crossings gate judges the deck; every other cause is an explanation of the gap and never an exemption from it.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

bury_or_undermine_over_the_moved_station.population: 489122 ZDOs in the save at 4366e0bc, 7262 measured prefabs
bury_or_undermine_over_the_moved_station.question: does the MOVED CARRIAGEWAY bury or undermine a standing build piece? delta_gate does NOT ask this - it measures GENERATED location content within 60 m - and ribbon's placed-object gate is on the BATTER alone, on the premise that the carriageway does not move. THIS WRITE MOVES IT, so the premise does not hold and the question is asked here.

repair_before.instrument: accept --section roads on ground from the SAVE (frozen copy), plus roads/applied.py::Applied.sample decode of the ledger's own blobs

plan_vs_last_emission.reference: reemit.compare_to_ground against the last profile-carrying terrain_write in the chain

approach_reach_solve.why: no claim on this segment, so there is no approach to solve

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle. A GAP IS JUDGED SEPARATELY AND IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: `step_into_m` is the worst adjacent-station rise walking from the last written rim THROUGH the gap to the first written rim after it, against the same slide limit scaled by the two stations' own separation - which is the climb out of an unwritten notch, NOT `step_across_m`, the two rims measured against each other. A bridged run is exempt because the ribbon must not write terrain there and the crossings gate judges the deck; every other cause is an explanation of the gap and never an exemption from it.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. rim_transfer.method: MEASURED on the 1 m lattice. Judged as a DELTA: a pair already over the limit is PRE-EXISTING and reported, never charged.
rim_transfer.rule: a write that TAKES ground must meet the ground at the RIM of what it takes. The closure is over DISPUTED samples and a rim sample nobody disagreed about is invisible to it, which is how a restitution moves its own cliff onto the segment it takes from instead of removing it.

water_sign.population: the 0 of 2 lattice sample(s) THIS WRITE MOVES whose GENERATED height is below the 30.0 m plane; of those, 0 are RAISED to or above it by this write and 0 were already above it and are not deepened

params.datum: an explicit CUT-ONLY lattice set: each named vertex is lowered to its own target height. NOT a datum and NOT a fitted profile -- a single datum held across a width is a cut at one edge and a fill at the other, which is why this write shape exists. The per-vertex targets are in `profile.nodes`

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. Judged as a DELTA: a pair already over the limit is PRE-EXISTING and reported, never charged.
rim_transfer.rule: a write that TAKES ground must meet the ground at the RIM of what it takes. The closure is over DISPUTED samples and a rim sample nobody disagreed about is invisible to it, which is how a restitution moves its own cliff onto the segment it takes from instead of removing it.

water_sign.population: the 2 of 2 lattice sample(s) THIS WRITE MOVES whose GENERATED height is below the 30.0 m plane; of those, 0 are RAISED to or above it by this write and 2 were already above it and are not deepened

params.datum: an explicit CUT-ONLY lattice set: each named vertex is lowered to its own target height. NOT a datum and NOT a fitted profile -- a single datum held across a width is a cut at one edge and a fill at the other, which is why this write shape exists. The per-vertex targets are in `profile.nodes`

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.half_width_m_is_zero_because: the tested set is the rasterised CARRIAGEWAY footprint -- every 1 m sample out to the road edge -- and violations_for_samples measures the MINIMUM distance from it to each instance, so a half-extent about those samples would count the road's own width twice
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.flatten_reason: over-water structure: its piles stand on the generated bed of an inland channel whose depth below the y=30 water plane this record does not declare and its deck stands at the road's own solved H 30.600 m. Levelling inside this footprint removes the water the structure is designed to stand in -- the measured early-dock defect -- and filling this channel to road freeboard would permanently drain it, which is the unrepairable direction (raising ground removes water).
